target.title: fix: sSH transport security check rejects connection before tunnel is established
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for configured remote Gateway SSH transport setup, URL safety, and managed tunnel lifecycle.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High. The branch has a live configured-SSH Gateway proof using a real foreground OpenClaw Gateway plus an isolated local OpenSSH daemon, focused regression coverage for Gateway call/bootstrap/status/logs/TUI/TTS/security-audit/doctor/devices/Crestodian paths, SSH launcher failures, status diagnostics, default SSH port handling, core/test-src typechecks, `git diff --check`, and a local ClawSweeper commit review with no actionable code finding.
- Root cause: The source-of-truth invariant for configured SSH remotes was split across URL validation, tunnel bootstrap, and status probing. Config-derived SSH remote URLs were treated as final plaintext `ws://` targets before the managed SSH tunnel could rewrite them to loopback, and some status paths reused the local tunnel port as the remote SSH destination port.
- Why this is root-cause fix: This fixes the source invariant rather than masking the symptom: config-derived SSH remotes that own tunnel startup are classified before plaintext validation, every owning client/probe path receives the loopback runtime URL after startup, and local listener ports are separated from remote Gateway destination ports. CLI/env overrides plus explicit `transport: "direct"` stay on the direct plaintext safety path.
- Reliability guardrails added: Owned SSH tunnels are closed on Gateway call/bootstrap failures, status/health/doctor probe completion or failure, and long-lived ACP/MCP/operator approval client shutdown. Status scans report SSH tunnel startup failures as an unreachable Gateway snapshot instead of aborting the whole status report.
- Compatibility guardrails added: Omitted `gateway.remote.transport` follows the documented SSH default when an SSH target is configured. Omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` keeps the documented remote-side default `18789`; configured URL/`--port` values remain local listener preferences unless explicitly used as the status command override. SSH spawn failures now reject through tunnel startup instead of becoming unhandled child-process errors.
- Existing CLI coverage retained: `openclaw logs` stays on the normal Gateway RPC client path for configured SSH remotes instead of failing in local-only preflight.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The canonical contract is `gateway.remote.transport` deciding direct vs managed SSH ownership, `gateway.remote.sshTarget` defining the managed tunnel target, `gateway.remote.remotePort` defining the remote Gateway destination port, and the configured Gateway URL/CLI `--port` defining the local listener preference. URL validation protects final direct network targets; SSH bootstrap owns transforming config-derived SSH targets into loopback runtime URLs.
- Scope boundary: The diff is limited to the configured Gateway SSH transport contract and the command/client surfaces that either start, diagnose, or hold a managed Gateway tunnel. ACP/MCP/operator approval files are touched only to release the tunnel that was handed to long-lived clients; provider routing, session storage, message delivery semantics, schemas, migrations, UI, and auth policy are not changed.
- Patch quality notes: Broad catches only suppress best-effort tunnel cleanup failures so they do not mask the primary startup/connect/status error already being returned. `null`/`undefined` default returns are fail-closed classification results for "no configured SSH tunnel owner" or "no SSH target" paths. Test `expect.any(...)` assertions cover framework-provided timing/object details while asserting the observable tunnel/auth/URL contract, and the timeout values changed in tests are command-budget inputs used to make probe behavior deterministic.
- Large diff / split check: This PR is larger than an ideal one-file fix because the broken invariant crossed validation, tunnel bootstrap, one-shot Gateway calls, long-lived clients, TUI chat, gateway-backed TTS, security audit, Crestodian overview, devices fallback, status/health/doctor probes, logs, ACP, MCP, and operator approval shutdown. Splitting would leave at least one user-visible caller with the old pre-tunnel rejection or leaked tunnel lifecycle; each touched surface is covered by focused regression tests.
- Related open PR / competition scan: daily-fix found the existing author PR #96134 for issue #26250 and switched to updating it instead of opening a duplicate. No separate competing implementation is being introduced here.
- What did NOT change: CLI/env Gateway URL overrides still use the existing plaintext safety check; explicit `transport: "direct"` remains direct connection mode; externally managed/manual tunnels without `sshTarget` still do not start a managed SSH process; no config migration, schema rewrite, or new transport protocol is introduced.
- Risk labels considered: security-boundary, compatibility, availability, and process lifecycle.
- Risk explanation: The main risk is accidentally widening plaintext `ws://` allowance beyond managed SSH ownership.
- Why acceptable: The allowance is limited to config-derived SSH remotes with SSH tunnel ownership; after tunnel startup the runtime client/probe URL is loopback, and tests cover direct transport, default SSH transport, missing `sshTarget`, tunnel cleanup, status diagnostics, remote-port defaulting, gateway-status port splitting, logs routing, and SSH spawn failure behavior.

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fixes #26250, where configured SSH transport could be rejected by the remote plaintext `ws://` security check before the tunnel was established.
- Ensures configured SSH remote Gateway clients and probes start the managed tunnel first, then connect through the local forwarded endpoint.
- Keeps documented SSH defaults intact: omitted `gateway.remote.transport` behaves as SSH when `sshTarget` is present, and omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` forwards to remote Gateway port `18789`.
- Makes status/diagnostic paths resilient when SSH tunnel startup fails, so users still get a status report with Gateway shown as unreachable.
- Keeps `openclaw gateway status` from forwarding the local tunnel listener port to the wrong remote Gateway port.

Why does this matter now?

Issue #26250 reports that the SSH transport security check rejects the connection before the SSH tunnel can be established. That blocks the documented safe remote Gateway setup even though the plaintext `ws://` URL is intended to become a loopback tunnel endpoint before client connection.

What is the intended outcome?

Configured SSH remote users can keep `gateway.remote.url` as the configured Gateway endpoint and `gateway.remote.sshTarget` as the SSH host. OpenClaw starts the tunnel, rewrites the runtime connection to the local forwarded endpoint, uses the documented remote port default, and cleans up the tunnel when the owning client/probe path finishes or fails.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This does not add a new transport protocol, change CLI/env URL override safety rules, make `transport: "direct"` bypass plaintext protection, or require a config migration. The scope is intentionally limited to configured Gateway SSH transport ownership and the surfaces that either start, diagnose, or retain that tunnel. It does not change provider routing, session persistence, message delivery semantics, auth policy, schemas, migrations, UI, or external manually managed tunnel behavior.

What does success look like?

A config-derived SSH remote starts a managed tunnel before client connection, default SSH transport works when `transport` is omitted, the remote side defaults to port `18789` when `remotePort` is omitted, direct transport remains explicit, status/logs paths share the same tunnel-aware contract, and diagnostic commands do not crash when SSH tunnel startup fails.

What should reviewers focus on?

Please focus on the ownership boundary for managed SSH tunnels: plaintext allowance is limited to config-derived SSH remotes, the runtime connection is rewritten to loopback immediately after tunnel startup, and tunnel cleanup remains tied to the owning Gateway client/probe path.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #26250

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #26250

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No direct maintainer request; this follows the public issue report.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Configured SSH remote Gateway URLs are no longer rejected before the managed tunnel path can run; tunnel setup rewrites the runtime URL to loopback; status diagnostics survive tunnel startup failure; default SSH transport and default remote-side port are preserved; `gateway status` no longer reuses the local listener port as the remote SSH destination port.
- Real environment tested: Real OpenClaw CLI process, real foreground OpenClaw Gateway process, and an isolated local OpenSSH daemon using strict host-key checking, public-key auth, token auth, and `ssh -L` direct-tcpip forwarding. The configured remote URL used a non-loopback TEST-NET-3 host so the proof exercises the same plaintext guard boundary as the issue report without relying on an external server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - Start an isolated OpenSSH daemon on loopback with a generated host key and generated client identity.
  - Start a real foreground OpenClaw Gateway on a separate loopback port with token auth enabled.
  - Configure the client profile with `gateway.mode: "remote"`, `gateway.remote.url: "ws://203.0.113.10:<localTunnelPort>"`, `gateway.remote.transport: "ssh"`, `gateway.remote.sshTarget`, `gateway.remote.sshIdentity`, `gateway.remote.remotePort`, and `gateway.remote.token`.
  - Run `openclaw gateway call health --json` through that config-derived SSH remote.
  - Run `openclaw gateway call health --url ws://203.0.113.10:<localTunnelPort> --token <token> --json` as the explicit override safety probe.
  - Run focused regression/type/diff checks listed in the validation section below.
- Evidence after fix (copied terminal output):

  ```text
  Configured remote URL: ws://203.0.113.10:34829
  SSH target: 127.0.0.1:42069
  Remote Gateway port: 35601
  Local tunnel preferred port: 34829
  configured SSH gateway call exit: 0
  configured SSH gateway status exit: 0
  explicit --url override exit: 1
  sshd accepted publickey: True
  sshd observed direct-tcpip forwarding to Gateway: True
  leftover OpenClaw ssh forward process: none
  ```

  ```text
  Configured SSH health response:
  ok: true
  JSON keys included: agents, channelLabels, channelOrder, channels, defaultAgentId, durationMs, eventLoop, heartbeatSeconds, modelPricing, ok, plugins, sessions, ts
  ```

  ```text
  Explicit --url override safety probe:
  Gateway call failed: Error: SECURITY ERROR: Gateway URL "ws://203.0.113.10:34829" uses plaintext ws:// to a non-loopback address.
  Both credentials and chat data would be exposed to network interception.
  Source: cli --url
  Fix: Use wss:// for remote gateway URLs.
  ```

  ```text
   RUN  v4.1.8 [local path redacted]

   Test Files  6 passed (6)
        Tests  369 passed (369)
     Duration  7.15s
  ```

  ```text
   RUN  v4.1.8 [local path redacted]

   Test Files  4 passed (4)
        Tests  71 passed (71)
     Duration  6.68s
  ```

  ```text
   RUN  v4.1.8 [local path redacted]

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  7 passed (7)
     Duration  1.06s
  ```

  ```text
  Validation result: pass, exit_code=0, 15479ms
  Validation result: pass, exit_code=0, 9527ms
  Validation result: pass, exit_code=0, 112ms
  ```

  ```text
  Focused sibling Gateway surface validation after local review:
  TUI Gateway chat: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 29 passed
  Gateway-backed TTS conversion: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 102 passed
  Security audit Gateway probe: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
  Doctor health Gateway diagnostics: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 49 passed
  Devices local fallback check: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 44 passed
  Crestodian overview Gateway probe: Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
  ```

  ```text
  After syncing with origin/main on 2026-06-28:
  pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/call.test.ts src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts src/gateway/ssh-transport.test.ts src/security/audit-gateway-ssh-transport.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts
  Test Files 10 passed (10)
  Tests 420 passed (420)
  Duration 51.74s
  ```

- Observed result after fix: The config-derived SSH remote opened an SSH session, sshd recorded public-key authentication and direct-tcpip forwarding to the real Gateway port, `openclaw gateway call health --json` returned `ok: true` through the configured SSH remote, and the managed tunnel process was gone after the CLI call completed. The explicit `--url` override with the same plaintext non-loopback URL still failed the plaintext safety check instead of receiving the configured-SSH exception.
- What was not tested: A public external SSH host was not used; the live proof used an isolated local OpenSSH daemon to avoid external credentials and network dependency while still exercising the real `ssh` binary, host-key checking, port forwarding, OpenClaw Gateway, and OpenClaw CLI.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The live proof runs the SSH server and Gateway on local loopback with generated keys/tokens, so it validates the transport lifecycle and safety boundary without proving internet routing, remote host firewalls, or a production SSH account configuration.
- Before evidence: Regression tests first failed because configured SSH `ws://` URLs hit plaintext validation before tunnel setup, omitted `remotePort` forwarded to the local URL port instead of `18789`, gateway-status forwarded local `19089` to remote `19089`, and SSH spawn errors surfaced as unhandled child-process errors rather than tunnel startup failures.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/ssh-transport.test.ts src/gateway/call.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-client.config.ts src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tui.config.ts src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-security.config.ts src/security/audit-gateway-ssh-transport.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-src.config.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/crestodian/overview.test.ts`

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Configured SSH transport opens a tunnel and rewrites the Gateway URL to loopback before client connection.
- Omitted `gateway.remote.transport` behaves as the documented default SSH transport when `sshTarget` is configured.
- Plaintext remote Gateway URLs are allowed only for callers that own the configured SSH tunnel.
- `openclaw logs` configured SSH remotes fall through to the normal Gateway RPC path and preserve tunnel-aware connection details when a transport error is reported.
- TUI Gateway chat starts the configured SSH tunnel before returning a remote Gateway URL, and stops it if remote auth resolution fails or Gateway client construction throws before ownership transfers to the chat client.
- Gateway-backed TTS conversion reads configured SSH Gateway details without tripping the pre-tunnel plaintext guard, rejects `--output` only for config-derived SSH remotes so it does not copy remote Gateway temp paths as local files, and still allows local loopback env overrides to write local output.
- Security audit and Crestodian overview Gateway probes start the configured SSH tunnel, probe the loopback URL, and stop the tunnel after probing.
- Security audit deep probes convert configured SSH tunnel startup failures into a failed Gateway probe warning instead of aborting the whole audit report.
- Doctor health auth-profile diagnostics can summarize configured SSH Gateway details without connecting or starting a tunnel.
- Devices local fallback checks do not replace Gateway pairing errors while inspecting configured SSH remotes.
- Call/bootstrap/status/health/doctor/ACP/MCP/operator approval paths clean up owned SSH tunnels on startup/connect failures.
- Status scans convert SSH tunnel startup failures into an unreachable Gateway snapshot instead of aborting the whole status report, and cold-start status paths can describe configured SSH remotes without starting a tunnel when network probes are skipped.
- Omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` forwards to remote Gateway port `18789`, while the config URL port remains the preferred local listener.
- `openclaw gateway status` passes separate local listener and remote destination ports to the SSH tunnel.
- SSH spawn failures reject through `startSshPortForward` instead of becoming unhandled child-process errors.
- POSIX SSH tunnel startup uses the trusted `/usr/bin/ssh` launcher instead of inherited `PATH` lookup; Windows keeps platform executable resolution.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- The issue reproduction path failed because the configured SSH remote URL was rejected by plaintext validation before tunnel setup.
- The default SSH transport regression test failed because `startSshPortForward` was not called when `remote.transport` was omitted.
- The logs configured-SSH regression test failed because the logs path rebuilt connection details without the configured SSH allowance.
- The sibling-surface regressions failed because TUI chat, gateway-backed TTS preflight, security audit, doctor health diagnostics, devices fallback checks, and Crestodian overview did not consistently apply the configured SSH allowance and tunnel ownership boundary.
- The configured-SSH gateway-backed TTS `--output` regression failed by trying to copy the Gateway process temp audio path as a local file after the managed tunnel path succeeded.
- The TUI auth-failure cleanup regression failed because the SSH tunnel could be started before remote auth resolution threw, leaving no returned client owner to stop it.
- The TUI construction-failure cleanup regression failed because `GatewayChatClient.connect()` returned ownership only after constructing the Gateway client; a constructor throw could leave the managed SSH tunnel running.
- The status regression test failed because tunnel startup errors rejected the whole status snapshot.
- The security audit deep-probe regression failed because SSH tunnel startup errors aborted the audit before `gateway.probe_failed` could be reported.
- The remote-port regression test failed because the remote SSH side inherited the local tunnel URL port.
- The gateway-status regression test failed because the status SSH probe used local `19089` as remote `19089` instead of remote `18789`.
- The SSH spawn regression test failed with an unhandled child-process error instead of a promise rejection.
- The POSIX SSH launcher regression failed because tunnel startup spawned bare `ssh`, allowing inherited `PATH` lookup instead of the trusted system SSH binary.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added or updated for the SSH transport default behavior, plaintext allowance scope, Gateway bootstrap/call paths, logs CLI behavior, tunnel cleanup paths, status diagnostics, gateway-status port splitting, remote port defaulting, and SSH spawn error handling.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Configured SSH remote Gateway users can now connect through the managed tunnel instead of being rejected before tunnel startup, and status/diagnostics handle tunnel startup failures more gracefully.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. The documented defaults for `gateway.remote.transport` and `gateway.remote.remotePort` are now honored in the managed SSH paths; no migration is required.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. The network path changes for configured SSH remotes, but the plaintext allowance is scoped to config-derived SSH remotes with tunnel ownership, and the final runtime target is loopback.

What is the highest-risk area?

Accidentally widening plaintext `ws://` allowance beyond the managed SSH tunnel ownership path.

How is that risk mitigated?

CLI/env URL overrides and explicit direct transport still use the existing plaintext safety check. Only config-derived remote URLs with configured SSH transport and an SSH target receive the allowance, and tests cover default SSH, direct transport, missing `sshTarget`, tunnel cleanup, status diagnostic failure, logs routing, gateway-status local/remote port splitting, remote-port defaulting, and SSH spawn failure behavior.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Ready for maintainer review after branch submission and CI.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

Author-side local validation and live configured-SSH Gateway proof are complete. The latest local ClawSweeper commit review found no actionable code finding; its remaining uncertainty was proof visibility in the local review context, which this PR body addresses with copied live proof and focused validation output. CI will rerun after branch submission.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

No maintainer review comments yet. ClawSweeper review findings are mapped explicitly:

- RF-001: The branch is ready for the waiting-on-author label to be re-evaluated after submission; author-side live proof, focused validation, and local commit review are complete.
- RF-002 / RF-006 / RF-007: Fixed the narrow TUI test mock lint blocker by replacing the constructor-only mock class and keeping the SSH tunnel mock scoped to configured-SSH tests.
- RF-003 / RF-008: Refreshed lint after the TUI mock repair; `corepack pnpm@11.2.2 lint --threads=8` passes.

target.title: fix(sessions): auto-generate session titles via AI summarization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where users with many saved sessions had to identify sessions from truncated first-message text or session-id style fallbacks, making session history harder to scan and search.

The previous generated-title work also needed the generated title to behave consistently across the gateway session list, search, session-change events, Control UI filtering/patching, and the agent-facing `sessions_list` tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an opt-in `sessionTitle` configuration and persists generated session titles as `autoTitle` metadata. Manual/display titles keep precedence, existing sessions without generated titles keep their current fallback behavior, and the feature remains default-off.

The title is derived from the same stored metadata across gateway, UI, and agent-facing session list paths. Background title generation uses the session model/auth context, not a separate public SDK selector path, and the public plugin SDK runtime-auth helper only accepts public parameters.

The update also avoids carrying transcript-derived generated titles into a new session after reset/new/rollover and guards async title writes so a title generated for an old `sessionId` is not written after the same `sessionKey` rotates to a new session.

Out of scope: manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, and new provider/channel/plugin capabilities.

## User Impact

When `sessionTitle.enabled` is on, users can get concise generated session titles instead of only first-message/session-id fallbacks. Session search can match those generated titles, already-open session lists can receive the post-write update, and agents using `sessions_list` see the same generated title users see.

Users who do not enable `sessionTitle` keep the existing behavior.

## Evidence

target.title: feat: add channel pairing request hook
target.body:
Related: #68214
Related: #89569

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can already approve pending DM pairing requests, but plugin authors do
not have a small, stable hook that fires when a new channel pairing request is
created. That makes common operator workflows harder than they should be:
notify the owner, write an audit record, open a ticket, or route the request to
an existing approval surface without polling pairing state.

Issue #68214 asked for an unauthorized/pre-auth hook surface, and review notes
there called the hook direction cleaner than adding one-off suppression config.
PR #89569 explores that broader access-request workflow, but it bundles the hook
with grouped allowlists, access-request behavior, trusted hook loading, command
changes, and channel-specific pre-auth message exposure. This PR keeps the first
step intentionally smaller: observe newly created pairing requests through the
shared pairing challenge path.

This does not close every ask in #68214: it does not expose allowlist-denial
events, add suppression semantics, or replace a future `message:unauthorized` /
access-denied hook. It is the narrower pairing-request notification primitive
that can land independently and coexist with a broader access-policy hook if
maintainers want that later.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed plugin hook, `channel_pairing_requested`, dispatched when a
channel DM pairing request is successfully created.

The hook is deliberately observation-only and narrow:

- no config/env surface
- no allowlist migration
- no auto-approval
- no custom denial/reply workflow
- no raw inbound message body, media, or transcript exposure

The event carries only the data a trusted plugin needs for notification/audit:
channel, optional account ID, channel-scoped sender ID, pairing code, and
sender-supplied channel metadata. Hook dispatch is fire-and-forget from the
pairing flow; failures remain fail-open, and the hook has a short default
timeout so slow notification plugins are bounded independently of the requester
reply. The code is a live, single-use approval credential and should only be
delivered to trusted operator sinks; metadata is untrusted display identity text.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can now build lightweight operator-notification workflows for new
DM pairing requests without polling the pairing store or patching individual
channels.

Because the event is emitted from the shared pairing challenge helper, channels
that already use the common pairing issuer get the hook through the central
path. Existing channel call sites now pass their resolved account IDs into that
shared issuer so multi-account notifications can identify the correct account.

This does not change default channel behavior for users without a plugin hook:
pairing requests are still created the same way, existing requests are not
re-emitted, and requester replies are still sent through the existing channel
flow.

target.title: fix #98158: Dashboard fails to load in Chrome v109 because Array.prototype.toSorted is not available
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Chrome v109 does not provide `Array.prototype.toSorted`, and the Control UI can call it during initial dashboard render.
- Solution: Install a focused Control UI entrypoint polyfill for `toSorted` and `toReversed` before `./ui/app.ts` loads.
- What changed: Added `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.ts`, imported it first from `ui/src/main.ts`, and added regression coverage for missing methods, native preservation, and import order.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Chrome v109 / Windows 7 users can open the dashboard instead of being blocked by an initial-render JavaScript exception.
- **What did NOT change:** No dashboard sorting policy, session data shape, gateway API, authentication flow, generated locale bundle, lockfile, or broad ES/Object polyfill surface changed.
- Fixes #98158

## What Problem This Solves

Chrome v109 / Windows 7 users can hit `toSorted is not a function` while opening the Control UI dashboard. Because the throw happens during app startup, the dashboard/login experience is blocked before the user can connect normally.

## User Impact

Users on the reported legacy browser can open the dashboard instead of being stopped by an initial-render JavaScript exception. Modern browsers keep their native array-copy implementations unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #98168 and #98247 are linked external open PRs for this issue.
- **Related open PR scan:** The linked open PR scan found #98168 and #98247; this body compares both same-issue competing PRs and keeps the scope canonical to the Control UI startup compatibility boundary.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #98168 only replaces the sidebar recent-session `toSorted` call, leaving the same missing-array-copy-method failure class in other Control UI runtime paths. #98247 takes a broad ES polyfill approach, but it changes more global APIs than the Chrome v109 blocker requires and currently has remote proof/lint failures.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** The compatibility boundary belongs at `ui/src/main.ts`, before any Control UI app module can evaluate. This patch installs only the two array-copy methods the UI uses for the reported failure class, preserves native methods, and avoids unrelated `Object`/`Array` global changes.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The proof launches the patched Control UI in a real browser process after removing `toSorted` and `toReversed` before navigation, then observes the entrypoint restores both methods and the page emits no array-copy-method or `TypeError` runtime errors.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Opening the Control UI when array copy methods are absent no longer throws before the dashboard/login screen renders.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux host, Vite dev server, `/usr/bin/google-chrome` driven by Playwright. Before navigation, the browser page set `Array.prototype.toSorted` and `Array.prototype.toReversed` to missing values so the app loaded through the legacy-method path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Started the Control UI dev server and drove system Chrome through the missing-method startup path.

```
pnpm --dir ui dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 58158 --strictPort

Playwright launched /usr/bin/google-chrome, removed Array.prototype.toSorted and
Array.prototype.toReversed before page navigation, then opened:
http://127.0.0.1:58158/
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Browser startup proof from the patched entrypoint:

```
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:58158/chat?session=main",
  "toSortedType": "function",
  "toReversedType": "function",
  "bodySnippet": "OpenClaw\n网关仪表盘\nWebSocket URL\n网关令牌\n密码 (不存储)\n连接\n协议不匹配\n提供的 Control UI 与正在运行的 Gateway 对支持的连接协议不一致。\n使用 openclaw dashboard 重新打开提供的 dashboard，确保 UI 和 Gateway 来自同一安装。\n如果使用 pnpm ui:dev，请基于当前 checkout 重新构建或重启开发 UI。\n更新 OpenClaw 后重启 Gateway，使其提供当前协议。\n原始错误\nControl UI 认证文档\n如何连接\n在主机上启动网关：\nopenclaw gateway run\n获取带令牌的仪表盘 URL：\nopenclaw dashboard\n将 WebSocket URL 和令牌粘贴到上方，或直接打开带令牌的 URL。\n查看文档 →",
  "errors": []
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The page reached the Control UI route, both array copy methods were functions after entrypoint evaluation, and the page produced no `toSorted`, `toReversed`, or `TypeError` runtime errors.
- **What was not tested:** Actual Chrome v109 on Windows 7 was not available. A live Gateway token connection was not used; the browser proof covers the startup/render boundary by removing the missing prototype methods before the Control UI entrypoint runs.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new issue-mode PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts` plus existing `ui/src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts` coverage.
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression test removes `toSorted` and `toReversed`, installs the entrypoint polyfill, checks non-mutating semantics, checks native preservation, and mocks `./ui/app.ts` to prove the fallback is installed before app evaluation.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A single call-site replacement would miss other Control UI array-copy-method usages, while broad ES polyfills would add unrelated behavior. The guardrail is entrypoint-level and limited to the missing array-copy methods.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch adds browser global prototype methods only when the browser lacks native `toSorted` or `toReversed`. Existing native implementations are left intact.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is limited to the Control UI entrypoint and one small polyfill module, with browser startup proof, production build verification, targeted tests, formatting, and lint coverage.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: unchanged.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The Control UI source-of-truth startup order in `ui/src/main.ts` imported `./ui/app.ts` before any compatibility setup; because Chrome v109 lacks `Array.prototype.toSorted`, startup/render code could call a missing method before the dashboard/login UI became usable.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix runs at the Control UI source-of-truth entrypoint before downstream app modules evaluate. That changes the startup invariant from "app code may run before array-copy methods exist" to "app code only runs after missing array-copy methods are installed or native methods are preserved."
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings are not symptom masking: the `Array.prototype` type escapes are limited to descriptor access for browser-native methods that may be missing at runtime, the mocked app module returns an empty ESM module only after asserting import order, there are no lint suppressions, no unrelated files, no lockfile changes, and the related open PR scan is addressed in the competition section.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `ui/src/main.ts` owns Control UI startup order; the patch fixes the compatibility contract before dashboard rendering, route setup, or other UI modules can consume array-copy methods.

## Additional verification

```
$ pnpm --dir ui test src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  79 passed (79)

$ pnpm --dir ui build
✓ built in 2.28s

$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.ts ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts ui/src/main.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.ts ui/src/array-copy-method-polyfills.test.ts ui/src/main.ts
RESULT: changed UI files oxlint passed
```

target.title: fix: OAuth refresh failures report reauth instead of stale success
target.body:
Closes #99120

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with managed OpenAI OAuth profiles could see auth appear healthy after a refresh failure when an external Codex CLI credential still existed but was stale or invalidated. This made operator status false-green and could require repeated pairing-code relogs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OAuth manager now fails closed on refresh errors instead of falling back to external CLI credentials after refresh failure. External CLI credentials remain available only for the existing unusable-profile bootstrap path.

Provider-wide auth discovery now also enforces that same ownership boundary: bootstrap-only Codex CLI `openai:default` is not synthesized as an automatic sibling candidate when a canonical local OpenAI OAuth profile already exists, unless that external profile was explicitly selected/configured.

Doctor and failed-turn refresh-failure hints include the affected safe profile id without mutating model defaults.

This touches CODEOWNERS auth files and likely needs auth/secops review.

## User Impact

Users and operators get an explicit reauth-required error for the affected profile instead of a misleading successful auth state. Doctor output and failed-turn guidance can point at the exact profile to relog without changing the user's default model.

## Review Response

Addressed the P1 review finding from `fuller-stack-dev` on head `66e088aff75f6727dc2c1754007d963fdceb6ad0`:

- `external-cli-sync.ts` no longer synthesizes runtime-only Codex CLI `openai:default` beside a named local OpenAI OAuth profile in provider-wide discovery.
- `resolveApiKeyForProvider` preserves the first typed `OAuthRefreshFailureError` while trying auth candidates and throws it when no earlier env/custom/synthetic fallback succeeds.
- `OAuthRefreshFailureError` carries a sanitized provider-prefixed `profileId`; `OAuthManagerRefreshError` passes it through with an explicit `override`.

target.title: fix(sessions): preserve trajectory on reset for outbound forensics (fixes #90707)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #90707.

On `/new` and `/reset`, OpenClaw archives the session transcript as `<sid>.jsonl.reset.<ts>` but the sibling **trajectory** file `<sid>.trajectory.jsonl` (the assistant's tool calls and tool results) and its `<sid>.trajectory-path.json` pointer are lost — overwritten when the session file path is reused, or left at their live names and then reclaimed by the lifecycle cleanup for the now-unreferenced old session id. For sessions that issued outbound communications, this makes post-incident forensics impossible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix mirrors the transcript-archive behavior for the trajectory in the shared reset path `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` (used by both reset entry points). Recent review also identified two P1 gaps:

1. **Env-free sibling preservation:** Sessions created before `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR` was enabled keep their live runtime next to the transcript, even when the pointer later names an override directory. Reset now archives both the current-env target and the env-free sibling.
2. **Constrained override cleanup:** The override directory is operator-configured, so the retention sweep now only removes files that carry a valid OpenClaw trajectory runtime header; unrelated archive-looking files are preserved.
3. **Unambiguous override archive names:** Override runtimes live as `<sessionId>.jsonl` inside `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`. If that directory overlaps with the sessions directory, a plain `.jsonl.reset.<ts>` archive would be discovered as a transcript archive. Override runtimes are now archived as `<sessionId>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.<ts>` so they are excluded by the existing trajectory classifiers.

### Retention and upgrade compatibility

- **No new retention code.** Reset-archived trajectories use the existing `.reset.<ts>` suffix and are pruned by the existing `resetArchiveRetentionMs` rule, so archive volume remains bounded.
- **Sensitive-data boundary.** Reset archives intentionally retain tool-call arguments and tool results for the configured retention window; this is the forensic purpose of the fix and matches the retention policy already applied to transcripts.
- **Backward compatible.** No existing file formats, database schemas, or session store layouts are changed. Existing sessions are unaffected until their next reset, at which point their trajectory is preserved instead of lost.
- **Operator-configured dir is read, not owned.** Adding `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR` to the cleanup scan only removes header-proven OpenClaw trajectory archives; it does not create new files or alter the directory's ownership semantics.

## User Impact

Reset-time session archives now retain the exact tool calls and tool results that preceded outbound actions, enabling post-incident forensics. Normal reset/delete behavior is otherwise unchanged, and no unbounded archive growth is introduced because the existing `.reset.<ts>` retention sweep prunes old trajectory archives.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Linux, Node 22, local `.mts` proof script driving the real `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` and `removeSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` production functions against real on-disk session directories.

**Fix (16 passed, 0 failed):**

  ok: sibling runtime archived
  ok: override reset archive has trajectory name
  ok: override reset archive is not plain .jsonl.reset
  ok: sibling reset archive exists

  ok: unrelated file preserved

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 16 passed, 0 failed

target.title: fix(discord): limit implicit reply references to first chunk
target.body:
Closes #99068

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with `replyToMode: "first"` could receive one native reply notification per physical chunk when a single long agent reply was split into multiple Discord messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now carries a source-aware first-chunk-only flag from outbound delivery into the shared send layer. The flag is only enabled for implicit single-use reply targets, so explicit `[[reply_to_*]]` replies and all-mode replies keep their existing reusable native reply behavior while the implicit turn reply no longer fans out across every physical text or media-caption chunk.

The payload send path now uses the same reply fanout contract for each physical Discord send, including `audioAsVoice`, native Discord payload media, and component follow-up media. That closes the reviewer-noted gap where one captured implicit reply id could be reused across voice/text/media sends.

The related open PR #99083 is not a strong blocker for this replacement shape: its current live review is still `status: needs proof` / `rating: unranked`, and ClawSweeper found that its mode-only suppression can break explicit first-mode chunk replies. This PR uses the reply source to avoid that compatibility regression.

## User Impact

Long Discord replies in first/batched implicit reply modes now quote the source message only on the first physical Discord message, avoiding repeated reply notifications for one logical answer. Explicit reply tags and all-mode replies remain reusable across chunks and payload sends as before.

## Evidence

- Claim proved on current head `71ae6b987eb7b5124e8921f7789ff96b865986ba`: Discord request bodies only include `message_reference` on the first physical chunk when the reply target is implicit single-use, while direct/default sends, explicit replies, and `replyToMode: "all"` keep their reusable native reply behavior.
- Claim proved on current head: the `audioAsVoice` payload path no longer captures and reuses one implicit reply id across voice/text/media physical sends; the regression now expects the voice send to keep the single implicit reply and the later text/media sends to omit it.
- Claim proved on current head: native Discord payload media sends propagate `replyToFirstChunkOnly: true` for implicit first-mode sends, so a direct payload send that internally chunks still suppresses trailing chunk native references.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts --reporter=verbose` passed: 3 files, 89 tests.

target.title: feat(xai): add realtime voice provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk already has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin did not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider.

Without this, users who want xAI/Grok voice in OpenClaw either cannot use it through Talk or have to fall back to a lower-quality STT -> model -> TTS loop. That is especially limiting for long-running assistants where supplier choice and realtime voice cost matter.

Closes #99087.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime voice provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract instead of creating a separate voice stack.

The provider:

- connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) over WebSocket;
- registers through the existing `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider` seam;
- exposes the provider through the xAI plugin manifest;
- maps audio, transcript, tool-call, cancellation, and close events into the existing Talk realtime bridge contract;
- keeps secrets out of docs and evidence.

The follow-up commits also address the ClawSweeper/Codex review findings: interrupted assistant audio is now paired with `response.cancel` plus `conversation.item.truncate`, the relay playback race preserves the assistant item until truncation is possible, and assistant transcript deltas are buffered so delta-only xAI completion still emits a final transcript.

Dependency note: `ws` is intentionally moved into the xAI runtime dependency set because the new provider imports it at runtime. The repository dependency guard correctly requires maintainer/security approval for the exact head SHA or a maintainer-owned regeneration path. This PR does not try to bypass that policy.

## User Impact

Users selecting xAI realtime Talk get native Grok voice replies through the existing OpenClaw Talk relay path rather than a synthetic STT/TTS loop.

Expected behavior:

- Talk can select `provider: "xai"` with `transport: "gateway-relay"`.
- Gateway-relay clients can stream mic audio and receive Grok voice audio.
- Barge-in cancels the active response and truncates only the currently interrupted assistant audio.
- Completed assistant audio and previous-turn assistant items are not truncated on later turns.

This is intentionally scoped to the xAI realtime voice provider and Talk relay integration. It does not weaken gateway auth and does not include secrets or production token values.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

No linked issue; this is a team-approved Android PR.

Android chat did not give users a discoverable way to start a fresh conversation or discover Gateway-backed slash commands from the composer. Earlier PR iterations also exposed session-command behavior that could diverge from the safer Control UI invariants: `/new` could travel through normal message send instead of Android's guarded New Chat path, and New Chat could still be available while active or queued chat work made a session switch unsafe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds Android New Chat controls backed by Gateway `sessions.create`, a Gateway-backed slash command picker that opens when users type `/`, prefix filtering by command name or text alias, and guarded handling for Android session creation. New Chat is disabled while sending, streaming, loading, running, or queued chat work is active; delayed `sessions.create` responses are ignored if the selected session or run state changed; selected or typed `/new` routes through the guarded Android New Chat path; and admin-gated slash commands Android cannot safely execute are filtered or disabled instead of requiring Android to request `operator.admin`.

Scope boundaries: Android does not request or persist `operator.admin`, this PR does not add a permanent slash button in the composer, and admin-gated reset execution is not part of the PR claim.

## User Impact

Android users can start a fresh chat from the header `+` action or with `/new` when chat state is safe. Typing `/` shows Gateway-backed command suggestions that narrow by command name or alias prefix, so Android no longer depends on a hard-coded fallback command catalog. target.title: fix(agents): claude-cli lifecycle cleanup — loopback fail-loud, exit-0 failover, bounded reseed, image sweep, one prepare cleanup owner
target.body:
Fixes #98946

## What Problem This Solves

Six lifecycle/cleanup defects in the claude-cli backend from the reliability audit — the tail of the same audit that produced #98933, #98934, #98942, and #98983:

1. A loopback MCP server startup failure was warn-and-continue: runs proceeded with bundled MCP enabled but no `openclaw` server, so agents ran whole turns with no messaging/gateway tools, and in `message_tool_only` delivery the visible reply was silently lost.
2. ~30 lines of dead "drain aborted turn" state in the live session (`drainingAbortedTurn`/`drainTimer`) — never activated since their introducing commit.
3. A live Claude process exiting 0 mid-turn produced a plain `Error`, bypassing failover entirely, while the identical one-shot outcome rotated the fallback chain via `FailoverError("empty_response")`.
4. Transcripts over 5MB silently disabled all reseed history (`return []`, parse errors swallowed) — and since claude-cli owns native compaction, long sessions can cross 5MB, after which any binding invalidation reseeded with zero context, unlogged.
5. CLI prompt image files were written content-addressed with a deliberate no-op cleanup, but no sweeper existed anywhere — unbounded disk growth per distinct inbound image.
6. Temp MCP-config and skills-plugin dirs leaked whenever preparation threw between backend prep and the two guarded regions (auth-epoch read, transcript probes, reference-path/sandbox/reseed stages were all unguarded).

## Why This Change Was Made

Bundled-MCP runs now fail loudly at prepare when the loopback server cannot start or publishes no runtime (no legitimate loopback-less bundleMcp mode exists — side questions and `disableTools` already skip bundled MCP). The dead drain machinery is deleted outright. Quiet exit-0/no-result live turns classify as `FailoverError("empty_response")`, attaching the `cli_unknown_empty_failure` retry code only when the turn observed no stdout activity — mirroring the one-shot path's gates rather than inventing looser ones. Oversized transcripts reseed from a bounded 5MB tail (first partial JSONL line dropped, session header preserved) and warn once on truncation or malformed lines. `writeCliImages` opportunistically sweeps files older than 7 days once per root per process (ENOENT-tolerant, debug-only on errors; the content-addressed path-stability contract is preserved — expired files are simply rewritten if needed again). Prepare cleanup now has a single try/catch owner covering every prepared resource from creation until ownership passes to the returned context, absorbing the two previous partial guards; the `beforeExecution` staging thunk from #98983 threads through the restructure unchanged. Fixes 2 and 6 together are LOC-negative in source (+456/−458).

## User Impact

Loopback failures surface as actionable errors instead of silently tool-less agents and lost replies. Mid-turn clean exits now take model fallback and recovery retries. Long-running sessions keep (bounded) reseed context instead of silently losing all of it past 5MB. Image-heavy deployments stop growing disk without bound, and failed preparations stop leaking temp directories.

## Evidence

- New/extended tests: loopback failure fails prepare; exit-0 classification with and without observed stdout; bounded-tail reseed including header preservation and malformed-line warning; image sweep TTL behavior; mid-prepare throw cleans the MCP temp dir and skills-plugin dir.
- Rebase proof over #98983: `git diff origin/main` is empty for that PR's landed test files (`bundle-mcp.test.ts`, `execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts`, `extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts`); `prepare.test.ts` differs only by this PR's own additive prepare-path tests.
- Validation on the rebased branch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` across prepare, spawn, session-history, helpers, reliability, execute supervisor-capture, bundle-mcp, and google setup-api suites (284 tests pass); extension-boundary import gate plus the boundary/tooling Vitest pair (94 tests) — the gates that caught #98983's first push; full remote `pnpm check:changed` green pre-rebase on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwgv54a1ak84zjy04pmesg8t` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28572651592, exit 0); repo autoreview (branch mode vs origin/main) clean.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: fix: clean up Android camera clips on cancellation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users running `camera.clip` could leave CameraX video use cases bound when the clip coroutine was cancelled or failed after binding the preview/video pipeline.

The affected workflow is remote camera video capture through the Android node app. A cancellation during warmup, recording delay, or finalization could skip the later success/error `unbindAll()` calls, leaving the camera session/resources active until another camera operation or lifecycle transition cleaned them up.

## Why This Change Was Made

The clip capture path now tracks the bound CameraX session, active `Recording`, and temporary MP4 ownership in one cleanup scope. A single `finally` path stops any still-active recording, unbinds the CameraX use cases, and deletes manager-owned temporary files while preserving successful clip files for `CameraHandler` to encode and delete.

The finalize wait now distinguishes the 15 second finalize timeout from coroutine cancellation, so cancellation can propagate while still running the same cleanup path.

## User Impact

Android camera clip requests no longer risk leaving the camera pipeline bound after interrupted or failed captures. Follow-up camera commands have a cleaner starting state, and cancelled/failed clips are less likely to leave temporary cache files behind.

## Evidence

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix: require Android contact and calendar write permissions in onboarding
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android onboarding could show Contacts or Calendar as authorized after only the read permission was granted, even though the app requests both read and write permissions from that row.

That left onboarding out of sync with the rest of the Android app: Settings already treats Contacts and Calendar as granted only when both read and write permissions are present, and the actual Contacts/Calendar add handlers require the write permission before they can create records.

This also fixes the filtered callback case. The onboarding request helper filters out permissions that are already granted before launching `RequestMultiplePermissions`; if READ was granted first and WRITE was granted later, the callback map can contain only WRITE. The state merge now uses the callback result plus the current system grant state for the omitted permission.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous onboarding state used only `READ_CONTACTS` and `READ_CALENDAR` for initial grant status, and the ActivityResult callback also only looked at those read permissions.

This change adds a focused read/write permission merge helper and uses it for Contacts and Calendar onboarding state. Initial state now requires both read and write permissions, and callback state now preserves already-granted permissions that were filtered out before the request was launched.

## User Impact

Users will no longer see Contacts or Calendar marked as ready in Android onboarding until the permissions needed by both read and add workflows are actually available. Users who grant the two permissions in separate prompts should now see the row update correctly once the missing permission is granted.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(irc): long non-ASCII messages are silently truncated at the 512-byte line limit
target.body:
Related: #42121

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long IRC replies written mostly in multi-byte scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, emoji) arrive cut off, losing a large part of every chunk with no error. The outbound chunker in `sendPrivmsg` splits text into chunks of 350 UTF-16 code units, but IRC caps a protocol line at 512 bytes including framing and CRLF (RFC 2812 section 2.3). 350 CJK characters encode to 1050 UTF-8 bytes, so each wire line is over 1000 bytes and the server silently truncates everything past byte 512. Issue #42121 reported this exact symptom for Chinese text; it was closed for the block-streaming delivery behavior, while the protocol-level byte overflow remained on main (`extensions/irc/src/client.ts:233`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`sendPrivmsg` now enforces a UTF-8 byte budget per chunk in addition to the existing character split. The budget is `512 - byteLength("PRIVMSG <target> :\r\n")`, derived only from the protocol line limit and the per-target framing overhead, and is deliberately independent of `messageChunkMaxChars`: the configured character cap keeps its meaning as a presentation preference applied by the first split, and the byte fit afterwards only enforces the wire limit. Because any single code point (at most 4 UTF-8 bytes) always fits the line budget, chunking always advances, including under very low character caps. The byte fit walks code points, so it never splits inside a surrogate pair, and it prefers breaking at the last space when one exists past half the fitted run, mirroring the existing character-split heuristic. ASCII behavior is unchanged (350 ASCII chars are 350 bytes, within budget).

`sendPrivmsg` is the single protocol choke point: the persistent monitor client and transient sends (`extensions/irc/src/send.ts`, `extensions/irc/src/monitor.ts`) both route through it. The upstream markdown chunker (`textChunkLimit: 350` in `extensions/irc/src/outbound-base.ts`) splits by characters for presentation and cannot know per-target framing overhead, so the protocol boundary is the right owner and no other surface needs changes.

The loopback IRC server used by the regression tests lives at `extensions/irc/test-support.ts`, the extension-local package-root test-support surface (same pattern as `extensions/browser/test-support.ts`), keeping raw socket use out of `extensions/irc/src` runtime paths and off the repo test-helper bridges that extension tests must not import.

Open PR #96572 touches the same loop but fixes a different defect (lone surrogates when the 350-code-unit split lands inside a surrogate pair) and adds no byte limit. The two changes are independent and compose; an adjacent-line rebase overlap is possible.

## User Impact

Long IRC replies in CJK, Cyrillic, emoji, or other non-ASCII text now arrive complete instead of losing the tail of every oversized chunk. ASCII messages chunk exactly as before, and operator-configured `messageChunkMaxChars` keeps its meaning, including low caps with multibyte text.

## Evidence

Live before/after driving the real production `connectIrcClient` (the same client used by the IRC channel's persistent and transient send paths) over a real loopback TCP socket. The only substituted component is the remote IRC server: a minimal loopback ircd that accepts registration and enforces the RFC 2812 512-byte line cap by truncating over-long lines exactly like a public network server. The client code, sanitizers, chunking, and socket I/O are all real, and both runs send the identical 900-character CJK message.

```
# BEFORE (pristine main a39b07bb15)
[BEFORE pristine main a39b07bb15] sent 1 message: 900 CJK chars (2700 UTF-8 bytes)
[BEFORE pristine main a39b07bb15] server received 3 PRIVMSG line(s):
  wire line 1070 bytes -> EXCEEDS 512, server truncated to 512
  wire line 1070 bytes -> EXCEEDS 512, server truncated to 512
  wire line 620 bytes -> EXCEEDS 512, server truncated to 512
[BEFORE pristine main a39b07bb15] text delivered to #general: 492/900 chars, 408 chars lost, intact=false

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
[AFTER this patch, identical inputs] sent 1 message: 900 CJK chars (2700 UTF-8 bytes)
[AFTER this patch, identical inputs] server received 6 PRIVMSG line(s):
  wire line 512 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
  wire line 512 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
  wire line 512 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
  wire line 512 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
  wire line 512 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
  wire line 260 bytes -> within 512, accepted whole
[AFTER this patch, identical inputs] text delivered to #general: 900/900 chars, 0 chars lost, intact=true
```

Regression tests (`extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts`) drive the same real client against a real loopback TCP server (`extensions/irc/test-support.ts`) with no mocks:

- CJK: every line fits 512 bytes and the full text is delivered.
- Emoji: byte limit honored with no lone surrogates per line.
- ASCII: chunk shape stays exactly [350, 350, 200], demonstrating preserved behavior.
- `messageChunkMaxChars: 100` with 250 CJK chars: chunk shape [100, 100, 50], demonstrating the character cap is honored and not shrunk to the byte budget.
- `messageChunkMaxChars: 2` with CJK text: chunking still advances ([2, 2, 2, 2, 2]) even though the cap is below one code point's UTF-8 byte count.

Validation on the changed files:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts`: 14 passed with the patch; the byte-limit and low-cap cases fail without it.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts`: 11 passed (the suite that flags banned repo test-helper bridge imports).
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-no-extension-test-core-imports.ts`: OK.
- The Critical Quality network boundary diff grep run locally against this branch's added lines under `extensions/irc/src`: no matches.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `tsgo` extensions production and test lanes: clean.

What was not tested: no session against a public internet IRC network, and the full build was not run (the change is internal to the IRC plugin).

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): skip IMDS during credential auto-detection (#64891)
target.body:
﻿## Summary

- Stop Bedrock memory auto-detection from probing AWS IMDS (`169.254.169.254`) when no AWS credential signals are configured.
- Keep the AWS SDK default credential chain available for explicitly selected/configured Bedrock memory providers, including shared config/profile, SSO, web identity, ECS, and EC2/IMDS role setups.
- During non-IMDS profile/container/web-identity probes, temporarily set `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` so `defaultProvider()` skips instance metadata while still resolving configured non-IMDS sources.
- Memoize `process.env` credential probes for 5 minutes and coalesce concurrent calls without sharing cached results across IMDS-enabled and IMDS-disabled probe modes.

Closes #64891

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Bedrock memory auto-detection no longer loads the AWS SDK credential chain, and therefore does not reach IMDS, when there are no AWS credential signals. Explicit Bedrock memory configuration still allows the full AWS SDK default chain.

Real environment tested: Windows local OpenClaw source checkout, running the patched Amazon Bedrock provider code directly through Node 22/tsx with AWS credential environment variables cleared.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

## Summary

- Keep diagnostic `message.queued` events for accepted active embedded-run steering without counting them as queued backlog.
- Apply the non-backlog accounting only to active embedded-run steering; reply-run fallback and normal queued messages still increment `queueDepth`.
- Add a regression test proving an active embedded run can accept steering, finish, and leave diagnostic `queueDepth` at zero.

## What Problem This Solves

Active embedded runs can accept steered messages immediately through their run handle. That path was still logged as queued backlog, incrementing diagnostic `queueDepth`.

When the active run later completed, the normal idle transition only decremented one queue slot, so diagnostics could still report positive `queueDepth` even though no queued work remained.

Fixes #98685

- The new regression test queues a message into an active embedded run, verifies the handle receives it, clears the run, and asserts diagnostic state is idle with `queueDepth === 0`.
